memory.content: All documentation entries must follow the standard format: Title, Definition, Key Attributes (bulleted list), Related Terms (links), and References section. Each entry should be concise and use industry-standard terminology.
EDI transaction documentation is top priority. All EDI documents (997, 204, 990, 850, 810) must include transaction code, purpose, business use case, and required/optional fields breakdown.
Use official industry terminology from NMFTA (National Motor Freight Traffic Association) standards and SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) guidelines. Avoid colloquial or regional terms.
Cross-reference related terms using relative markdown links. Link to parent category in each entry (e.g., LTL entries link to modes/, EDI entries link to edi/).

Knowledge base organized into 7 top-level categories: modes/ (shipping modes), edi/ (EDI transactions), terms/ (general terminology), parties/ (stakeholders), locations/ (geography), packaging/ (units), financials/ (cost structures). Each new entry must fit one category.
All documentation must be verifiable against official sources. Include reference links to NMFTA, ANSI X12, or carrier-specific documentation. No speculative or opinion-based content.

memory.summary: How FrieghtKB chooses a top-level documentation folder for a new entry.
memory.content:
# Categories:

1. modes/ - Transportation methods (LTL, FTL, Parcel, Intermodal, Break Bulk, Air, Ocean)
2. edi/ - EDI transaction sets (997, 204, 990, 850, 810)
3. terms/ - General terminology (Stops, Route Optimization, Accessorials, Demurrage, SCAC)
4. parties/ - Stakeholders (Shipper, Carrier, Consignee, Forwarder, Broker, 3PL)
5. locations/ - Geographic info (Address Formats, Ports, Terminals, Distribution Centers)
6. packaging/ - Handling units (Pallets, Containers, Crates, Drums)
7. financials/ - Cost structures (FTL Charges, LTL Rates, Accessorial Charges, Fuel Surcharges)

# Placement Logic:
- HOW freight moves? → modes/
- X12 transaction? → edi/
- WHO (stakeholder)? → parties/
- WHERE (location)? → locations/
- Packaging type? → packaging/
- Cost/billing? → financials/
- Otherwise → terms/

memory.summary: Filename and capitalization conventions used when adding FrieghtKB markdown entries.
memory.content:
# Naming Rules:

## General:
- Extension: .md
- Simple terms: no spaces (use PascalCase)
- Compound industry terms: preserve spaces
- Match official capitalization

## By Category:
- edi/: [code].md (e.g., 997.md, 204.md)
- modes/: [ModeName].md (e.g., LessThanTruckLoad.md)
- terms/: [Term Name].md (e.g., Route Optimization.md)
- parties/: [PartyRole].md (e.g., Customs Broker.md)
- locations/: [LocationType].md (e.g., Formats.md)
- packaging/: [Unit Name].md (e.g., Handling Units.md)
- financials/: [Cost Type].md (e.g., FTL Charges)

## Special:
- Avoid: / \ : * ? " < > |
- Each category has README.md
- Root has README.md entry point

memory.summary: Which authorities FrieghtKB cites and which sources are disallowed.
memory.content:
# Primary Standards:

1. NMFTA (nmfta.org) - Motor carrier, SCAC codes, classifications
2. ANSI X12 (x12.org) - EDI transaction standards
3. IATA (iata.org) - Air freight standards
4. IMO (imo.org) - Ocean shipping regulations

# Secondary:
- Carrier documentation (FedEx, UPS, USPS)
- Trade associations (IANA, TIA)
- Government agencies (DOT, CBP)

# Process:
1. Check primary standards body
2. If not found, check carrier/association docs
3. If conflicts, note discrepancy
4. Always cite source with URL
5. Prefer recent publications

# Prohibited:
- Wikipedia (verify with authoritative source)
- General dictionaries
- Blog posts
- Outdated docs (>5 years)

skills.name: doc-entry
skills.description: Standard workflow for adding new documentation entries to FrieghtKB
skills.content:
# Documentation Entry Workflow

## Purpose
Add a new FrieghtKB documentation entry in the correct category with the standard template.

## Use when
- A new term, mode, party, location, package, financial item, or EDI set needs an entry.

## Do not use when
- Expanding the category taxonomy itself; deprecating an existing term.

## Inputs
- The term to document; the seven top-level folders (modes/, edi/, terms/, parties/, locations/, packaging/, financials/).

## Procedure
1. Identify category: determine which top-level folder fits (HOW freight moves → modes/; X12 transaction → edi/; WHO → parties/; WHERE → locations/; packaging type → packaging/; cost/billing → financials/; otherwise → terms/).
2. Create the file using the category naming rule: PascalCase for multi-word files, edi uses [code].md, and preserve official capitalization and spaces for compound industry terms.
3. Apply the template: H1 title, Definition paragraph, Key Attributes section, Related Terms section, References section.
4. Verify terminology against NMFTA/ANSI (or IATA/IMO when those bodies apply); cite a URL; do not use Wikipedia, blogs, or docs older than five years as the authority.
5. Link bidirectionally: add at least two related-term links and update those related entries to link back.
6. Commit with format: Create [TermName].md after the quality checks pass.

## Quality checks
- File in correct category folder
- Industry terms properly capitalized
- At least 2 related terms linked
- At least 1 authoritative reference

## Constraints
- No speculative or opinion-based content.

skills.name: edi-doc
skills.description: Specialized workflow for documenting EDI transaction sets
skills.content:
# EDI Documentation Workflow

## Purpose
Document an EDI transaction set with the mandatory sections and X12 naming.

## Use when
- Adding or revising an entry under edi/.

## Do not use when
- General terminology that is not an X12 transaction.

## Inputs
- The X12 transaction code, ANSI name, and implementation-guide URL.

## Procedure
1. Record Transaction Code: the X12 number, and name the file [code].md (for example 997.md, 204.md).
2. Record Official Name: the ANSI X12 standard name; title the page as EDI [code] - [name].
3. Record Purpose: the business workflow role of the transaction.
4. Record Direction: Sender to Receiver.
5. Record Required Fields as a mandatory segments table, then Optional Fields as common optional segments.
6. Add 2-3 Business Scenarios and Related Transactions that link the workflow chain.
7. Link to ANSI X12 documentation and include the implementation guide URL.

## Verification
- All mandatory sections are present; file name is the X12 code; references resolve.

## Constraints
- Do not document an EDI set in terms/ or another category.

skills.name: category-expand
skills.description: Process for adding new documentation categories
skills.content:
# Category Expansion Process

## Purpose
Add a new top-level documentation category only when the existing seven cannot hold the entries.

## Use when
- A proposed topic does not fit modes/, edi/, terms/, parties/, locations/, packaging/, or financials/.

## Do not use when
- The topic fits an existing folder; adding a single entry.

## Inputs
- The proposed category name, purpose, and candidate entries.

## Procedure
1. Check whether the topic fits the existing 7 categories using the placement logic (how / X12 / who / where / packaging / cost / otherwise terms).
2. Verify at least 5 entries would justify a new category.
3. Propose the category in an issue or discussion and wait for approval.
4. If approved: create the directory with README.md covering purpose, scope, entry criteria, and naming conventions.
5. Update the root README.md, seed with 3 initial entries, and update related entries with cross-links.
6. Commit as: Add [category]/ with [n] entries.

## Verification
- README states purpose and naming; at least 3 seed entries exist; root README lists the folder.

## Constraints
- Do not add a category for fewer than 5 justified entries.

skills.name: link-check
skills.content:
# Link Validation Workflow

## Purpose
Validate and repair FrieghtKB cross-references.

## Use when
- After moves, new entries, or a reported broken link.

## Do not use when
- Writing a first draft that has not been placed yet.

## Inputs
- The category tree and the changed files.

## Procedure
1. Check that internal links resolve to existing files.
2. Check that category backlinks are present.
3. Check that related-term links are bidirectional.
4. Check that external references return HTTP 200.
5. Fix by updating moved file paths, adding missing backlinks, and replacing dead URLs with alternatives from NMFTA/ANSI/carrier docs.
6. Document the repair in the commit message: Fix broken links in [category]/.

## Verification
- Internal links resolve; related terms point both ways; external URLs respond.

## Constraints
- Do not delete a historically referenced file solely because a link broke.

skills.name: term-deprecate
skills.content:
# Term Deprecation Workflow

## Purpose
Retire outdated terminology without losing history or external references.

## Use when
- A term is replaced by a newer official name.

## Do not use when
- Correcting a typo in a still-current term.

## Inputs
- The old term file, the replacement entry, and incoming links.

## Procedure
1. Keep the old file for history; do not delete it in the deprecation commit.
2. Add a deprecation notice at the top pointing to the replacement.
3. Update incoming links to the replacement.
4. Add a redirect note in the category README.
5. Remove the old term from main navigation.
6. Retain the file for 1 year, then move to archive/; never delete if it is externally referenced.
7. Commit as: Deprecate [OldTerm] in favor of [NewTerm].

## Verification
- Old file still exists with a notice; navigation no longer lists it; incoming links go to the replacement.

## Constraints
- Never delete an externally referenced term.

skills.name: i18n-doc
skills.content:
# Internationalization Workflow

## Purpose
Add a regional documentation variant only when terminology or regulation actually differs.

## Use when
- Canada, Mexico, EU, or Asia-Pacific usage differs from English (US).

## Do not use when
- Minor spelling differences (for example color/colour).

## Inputs
- The base English (US) entry and the regional difference to record.

## Procedure
1. Confirm a variant is warranted: terminology differs significantly, legal/regulatory requirements differ, or industry practices vary — not minor spelling.
2. Name the file [Term]_[region].md.
3. Include the standard template sections and add a Region field.
4. Highlight a Regional Differences section.
5. Link to the base entry and to other variants.

## Verification
- Variant file uses the regional suffix; base and variant link to each other; differences are explicit.

## Constraints
- Primary language remains English (US); do not fork a page for spelling-only changes.
